summary: d12dd96 adds resizeDetector (top/ui.go) and wires exactly one repaintStored call into layout's final block, satisfying every task-07 acceptance criterion I could verify mechanically and by reading current top/ui.go, top/pause.go and the vendored gocui@v0.5.0 source. Both implementer deviations (no sizeChanged wrapper, no duplicate latch test) are correct calls, not shortcuts: the task file's own TDD Anchor and Details sections override the stray 'What to do' bullet, and task 03's Test_repaintFailureLatch_reportsOncePerTransition already discharges the AC. No critical or major findings; one optional stylistic nit.

suggestions.suggestion: The three 'facts a reader cannot recover from the code' are stated twice: once in the resizeDetector type doc comment (lines 186-204) and again, compressed, in the inline comment above the observe() call inside layout (lines 328-333). Consider trimming the inline comment to a one-line pointer back to the type doc rather than re-deriving the same three points.
suggestions.benefit: Slightly less to keep in sync if the rationale ever changes; purely cosmetic, matches the file's existing habit of heavy 'why' comments elsewhere (e.g. the extra-panel block) so it is not out of place.

verifiedInvariants.resizeDetector_touches_only_pause_and_in: confirmed - observe(paused bool, x, y int) bool; no app, no gocui reference anywhere in the type or method (top/ui.go:205-223)
verifiedInvariants.state_lives_in_layout_enclosing_closure: confirmed - 'var resize resizeDetector' at top/ui.go:232, inside func layout(app *app) but outside the returned func(_ *gocui.Gui) error closure, same register as verboseTooShortShown (line 229). mainLoop calls layout(app) fresh on every Gui rebuild (top/ui.go:62), so the closure and its captured resizeDetector are recreated with zero value each time - verified this is what fires the post-pager repaint via Test_resizeDetector_observe's 'zero start state' subtest
verifiedInvariants.zero_geometry_guard_precedes_detector: confirmed - guard 'if maxX == 0 || maxY == 0 { return fmt.Errorf("") }' at top/ui.go:239-241 returns before the detector call at line 334-336; a 0x0 post-pager size can never reach observe()
verifiedInvariants.layout_still_returns_nil_no_new_error: confirmed - detector call sits inside a plain if with no error return; layout's final statement is unconditional 'return nil' (top/ui.go:338)
verifiedInvariants.exactly_one_new_repaintStored_call: confirmed - top/ui.go has 2 repaintStored(app) call sites: line 129 (pre-existing, task 03's statLoop wiring in doWork) and line 335 (new, this task); grep count of 3 includes one explanatory comment mention at line 330
verifiedInvariants.file_scope_respected: confirmed - `git show d12dd96 --stat` touches only top/ui.go (+52) and top/ui_test.go (+96); top/pause.go, top/stat.go, top/dialog.go untouched by this commit (dialog.go was touched by the separate 32d557a / task 08 commit, correctly out of scope here)
verifiedInvariants.no_task09_logtail_seam: confirmed - no logBuf/logPath/logtail references anywhere in the d12dd96 diff
verifiedInvariants.gocui_technical_claims_verified_against_: confirmed against /home/lesovsky/go/pkg/mod/github.com/jroimartin/gocui@v0.5.0/gui.go: handleEvent (lines 409-417) dispatches only EventKey/EventMouse (to onKey) and EventError, default falls through; flush() (lines 421-434) reads termbox.Size() and assigns g.maxX/g.maxY BEFORE calling managers' Layout; Gui.Update (line 311-313) is a 3-line goroutine-spawning channel send with no lock; MainLoop's userEvents case (lines 377-379) returns any error from ev.f(g) out of MainLoop itself - all match the code comments' claims exactly

deviationAssessment.a_no_sizeChanged_helper: Correct per task instruction. The task's own 'What to do' section explicitly says 'One layer, not two... Do not add it' referring to sizeChanged, calling out this exact tech-spec wording mismatch as an expected, pre-approved naming deviation to record in the decisions log, not a defect.
deviationAssessment.b_no_new_latch_test: The task file genuinely self-contradicts: the 'What to do' bullet says to add a covering test for the latch in top/ui_test.go, while the TDD Anchor ('The failure latch is NOT tested here... Rely on Task 3's coverage') and the Details section ('The latch is not yours to build... Do not add a latch test of your own: Task 3's Test_repaintFailureLatch_reportsOncePerTransition already covers it, and a same-prefix test here would make this task's -run pattern pass without any work being done') both explicitly forbid it, with the Details section additionally spelling out a hazard the AC's isolated wording does not: a poorly-chosen test name here could shadow the real coverage under a shared -run prefix. I read the 'What to do' bullet as leftover text from an earlier draft (the same category of staleness the task file already flags for sizeChanged), and the twice-repeated, more specific instruction as authoritative. I independently confirmed top/pause.go (commit 8ae86f3) ships recordRepaint as a separately callable method on frameStore and top/pause_test.go carries Test_repaintFailureLatch_reportsOncePerTransition with exactly the fail/fail/fail/success/fail -> true/false/false/false/true sequence the anchor describes. The acceptance criterion's actual wording - 'is covered by a test proving exactly one cmdline message per failure transition' - does not require the test to live in this commit's diff, only that coverage exists; it does. The implementer's judgment call is correct and the AC is genuinely satisfied without new code.
